passage: Zeynep drew a table on a big sheet in the corridor of her school in Istanbul: Decoration, Music, Food, Invitations. Beside each, one name and a date. Decoration: Aiko, by Thursday. Music: Emre, playlist by Friday morning. Food: Lucas, list to the teacher by Wednesday. Invitations: Zeynep herself, printed by Tuesday. "Not 'the team,'" she said, capping her marker. "One name each." Aiko grinned. "So if the paper lanterns fail, it's my fault." "And if they work?" "Then it's my glory." On Wednesday Lucas handed in the food list, and on Thursday Aiko arrived with two boxes of lanterns. Only the music slipped by a day, and Zeynep knew exactly whom to ask.

qa.q: Who was responsible for decoration and by when?
qa.a: Aiko was responsible for decoration, by Thursday.

qa.q: How does Aiko feel about owning the lanterns?
qa.a: Aiko feels cheerful and willing to take responsibility, joking that failure would be Aiko's fault and success Aiko's glory.

qa.q: What could Zeynep add to the plan if a task slips, and why?
qa.a: Zeynep could add a short check-in a day before each date, because an early reminder catches slips while there is still time to fix them.

qa.q: How might Emre see having a named task?
qa.a: Emre knows exactly what is expected and by when, so a slip is Emre's to fix and no one else is left guessing.

grounding: Tasks are split into decoration, music, food and invitations, each assigned to one named person with a date, so nothing depends on everyone thinking someone else will do it.

passage:
The Class 9 Diwali party was eight days away when Hemant pinned a sheet on the notice board outside the staff room.

"Four jobs, four names, four dates," he told the group. "Decoration: Samir, sample colours by Tuesday. Music: me, playlist to Ma'am by Thursday. Food: Leela and Joshua, final list Wednesday. Invites: Parveen, cards in every class by Monday."

Samir frowned. "Last year we just said 'everyone helps'."

"And last year nobody bought plates, because everybody thought somebody else had." Hemant tapped the sheet. "If your date slips, you tell me that same day. No shame, we just fix it."

On Tuesday Samir showed up with swatches. On Wednesday the food list was short by juice, and Leela added it before lunch. The party wasn't perfect, but every job had someone.

qa.q: Who was responsible for the invitations?
qa.a: Parveen was responsible for the invites, with cards in every class by Monday.

qa.q: Why did Samir frown at first when Hemant read out the jobs?
qa.a: Samir seemed unsure and a little resistant, because the year before they had simply said everyone helps and the new system felt stricter.

qa.q: What could Hemant add to make the plan even safer?
qa.a: He could add a second name as backup for each task, so one absent person would not stall a whole job.

qa.q: How does the plan look from the class teacher's side?
qa.a: The teacher knows exactly whom to ask about each part, and gets the playlist on a fixed day, which makes the party easier to supervise and trust.

grounding: Shows party tasks split into areas, each given to one named person with a date, so nothing is left to everyone assuming someone else will do it.

passage:
Dear Gurpreet,

You asked how our building's Lohri night went. Honestly? Better than any year before, and I think I know why.

Last time, the uncles said "everyone pitch in", and we ended with three bags of peanuts and no firewood. This year I made a list on the lift door: firewood, Pinky Aunty's son, by Friday; music, me, by Saturday; food, the Arora twins, by Sunday; invites, the Kaur sisters, through the building chat group, by Thursday.

Everyone could see their own name in marker. When the twins realised they'd forgotten jaggery, they fixed it themselves, because it was clearly theirs to fix.

I'm tired but happy. Next year you're getting a line on that list too, so come early!

Mohit

qa.q: Where did Mohit put the list of tasks?
qa.a: Mohit made the list on the lift door.

qa.q: How does Mohit feel after the Lohri night?
qa.a: Mohit feels tired but happy, and a little proud, because the event went better than any year before.

qa.q: What else could Mohit try next year to make handovers smoother?
qa.a: Mohit could hold a short check-in two days before the event, so owners can flag problems like the missing jaggery even earlier.

qa.q: How might the Arora twins have experienced having their names on the list?
qa.a: They probably felt responsible and trusted; since the food was clearly theirs, they fixed the jaggery themselves instead of waiting for someone else.

grounding: A letter describing an event where each task had one named owner and a date, so people did not assume others would do it.
